editorial:
Imagine a world where people are so obsessed with celebrities that they actually pay to get the same sicknesses as their idols. That is the wild setup you get here. You follow Syd, a guy who works at a clinic that sells these virus injections. The whole vibe is cold, clean, and honestly a bit gross. It feels like a nightmare where fame has gone totally wrong. You will see people risking their lives just to feel a connection to a star, which makes the whole thing feel creepy and strange from the start.

What really hits is how the movie looks and the weird tension it builds. The acting is solid, though the story moves a bit slow at times. If you hate seeing needles or skin rashes, you might want to look away. However, if you like stories that make you think about how weird our current fan culture is, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the end, you find out that the clinic was lying about the viruses. Syd discovers that the sicknesses are not actually coming from the stars, but are being made in a lab. He realizes he was just a pawn in a big game. The movie wraps up with Syd becoming the new object of obsession. He ends up as the sick celebrity that other fans now want to copy, completing a dark cycle.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange stories about the dark side of fame.
